slides.teacher_cue: New sound. Tongue tip touches the ridge behind the upper teeth — like /d/ — then releases with friction. A combination of stop and fricative. Voice on. j-j-j. Korean has a similar sound — ㅈ — so production is generally accessible.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /dʒ/ cleanly as a voiced postalveolar affricate.
slides.correction_move: Model the two parts: /d/ position, then release into friction. Students copy. Contrast with /g/ — both voiced stops but /j/ has the friction release.
slides.observation_note: Watch for any confusion with /g/ or devoicing to /tʃ/.
